title: Why Meta's Muse AI agent feels different after volatile stock stretch
excerpt: Meta's Muse agent gives investors new evidence its expensive AI push could become a real, transformative business.
content_html:
If you've been a Meta shareholder for the entirety of 2026, you've been on a wild ride.

Investors have repeatedly flipped on a dime from AI optimism to concerns over spending. Earnings have usually brought a huge stock move — but the direction has been hard to predict. That's made the nearly $2 trillion Meta one of the market's most volatile mega-cap stocks, facing the kind of turbulence usually reserved for smaller companies.

Meta's latest surge has been powered by the rapid uptake of Muse, its personal AI agent, since it was released on Sept. 8. The stock's response suggests investors see the app as the company's clearest shot yet at turning its enormous AI investment into a meaningful new business.

The chart above shows the tug-of-war that has defined Meta's year, leaving shares up 18% year to date through Thursday. Wall Street repeatedly balked at the price of its AI ambitions, only to warm up when a potential payoff came into view.

But Muse gives investors more than another promise about what AI might someday do for Meta. It offers a glimpse of the holy grail: a tangible example of what the company can build — and potentially sell — with all that spending.

Why this time feels different

The rise of agents could be a genuine inflection point for AI, marking a shift from simply answering prompts to carrying out tasks. Meta has an early opening to lead the consumer side of that next phase.

Andrew Boone, an analyst who covers the stock for Citizens, sees Muse entering the grand pantheon of AI breakthroughs (emphasis mine):

"With Muse appearing to reach the next AI inflection point, the same way Claude Code did for enterprise AI last winter, and ChatGPT did originally with Chatbots, Meta is increasingly well positioned to grow share of consumer AI usage," he said in a Thursday report.

His peers seem to agree. JPMorgan analysts raised their price target on Meta by $100, while Raymond James went one better and hiked by $210 — hefty moves for a stock already trading in triple digits.

One advantage consistently cited by Meta bulls is the company's massive built-in audience. Its family of apps already reaches billions of people every day. If even a sliver of them become regular users of Muse or agentic-AI devices like its new Charm dongle or its $1,300 VR Glasses, Meta could establish a big early lead.

At the moment, it amounts to a two-pronged first-mover advantage: (1) a head start in consumer-AI hardware and (2) an audience that rivals would spend a fortune to reach.

Zuck is thinking big, per usual

For those who dare to dream even bigger — Mark Zuckerberg chief among them — Muse represents an attempt to build the next big consumer tech platform. It's hard to imagine a world where Apple's iOS isn't top dog, but Meta is going to try. It's betting that talking to wearables or personal devices could replace scrolling and tapping a phone screen.

It's a bold bet, and one that still has miles to go before it becomes full-fledged reality. But in the market, investors are already buying in. That stock spike in the Meta chart above is bigger and faster than any it's seen this year.

It's too early at this point to know how the agentic-AI race will play out. There's not even a guarantee that it'll remain a dominant theme at all. But in a market that gets easily whipped into a frenzy, Meta is the next great hope … for this week at least.
